# Evidence Loom for After-Hours Dental Lab Master Spec Prompt

Build Evidence Loom for After-Hours Dental Lab as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for after-hours dental lab.
Use Evidence Loom as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic health templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: weaves scattered proof into a single inspectable decision trail for after-hours dental lab, using case trays, shade photos, and remake approvals.
- Primary workflow: intake night-shift ceramic crown remakes into a photo proof set while respecting offline-capable constraints
- Signature interaction: drag evidence chips into a timeline and watch missing links glow

## Required Shape
- First screen: Photo Proof Set workbench
- Hero controls: Intake, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: case trays, shade photos, and remake approvals

## Service Boundary
- Keep photo proof set state in a service; UI submits intake commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Evidence Loom for After-Hours Dental Lab' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: offline-capable workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for after-hours dental lab and keep Evidence Loom as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Photo Proof Set workbench and keep the visible controls to Intake, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Photo Proof Set workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep photo proof set state in a service; UI submits intake commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for case trays, shade photos, and remake approvals so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of offline-capable workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Evidence Loom for After-Hours Dental Lab' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Evidence Loom for After-Hours Dental Lab to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for intake and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

Build Friction Map for After-Hours Dental Lab as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for after-hours dental lab.

- Keep dispatch ticket state in a service; UI submits assemble commands and subscribes to progress.

- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Agents

- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

Build Scenario Forge for Microgreen Farm Co-Op as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for microgreen farm co-op.
Use Scenario Forge as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic agriculture templates.

- Why this exists: builds small what-if trials before committing to a plan for microgreen farm co-op, using chef demand, tray growth stages, and delivery slots.
- Primary workflow: assemble harvest promise matching into a route manifest while respecting evidence-linked constraints
- Signature interaction: scenario tabs that compare assumptions side by side

- First screen: Route Manifest workbench
- Hero controls: Assemble, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: chef demand, tray growth stages, and delivery slots

- Keep route manifest state in a service; UI submits assemble commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Agents
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Scenario Forge for Microgreen Farm Co-Op' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: evidence-linked workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces, Agents with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Scenario Forge for Microgreen Farm Co-Op' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Scenario Forge for Microgreen Farm Co-Op to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for assemble and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

Build Pocket Ops Room for Eldercare Ride Circle as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for eldercare ride circle.
Use Pocket Ops Room as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic health templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: compresses a full back office into a field-ready workflow for eldercare ride circle, using mobility notes, appointment windows, and consent.
- Primary workflow: monitor trusted driver coordination into a route manifest while respecting evidence-linked constraints
- Signature interaction: offline-first job packet with later sync review

## Required Shape
- First screen: Route Manifest workbench
- Hero controls: Monitor, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: mobility notes, appointment windows, and consent

## Service Boundary
- Keep route manifest state in a service; UI submits monitor commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Automations, Settings
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Pocket Ops Room for Eldercare Ride Circle' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: evidence-linked workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for eldercare ride circle and keep Pocket Ops Room as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Route Manifest workbench and keep the visible controls to Monitor, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Route Manifest workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep route manifest state in a service; UI submits monitor commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for mobility notes, appointment windows, and consent so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of evidence-linked workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces, Automations, Settings with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Pocket Ops Room for Eldercare Ride Circle' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Pocket Ops Room for Eldercare Ride Circle to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for monitor and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

# Route Whisperer for Maker-Space Tool Library Master Spec Prompt

Build Route Whisperer for Maker-Space Tool Library as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for maker-space tool library.
Use Route Whisperer as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic developer-tools templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: turns conflicting constraints into a ranked route or assignment for maker-space tool library, using training status, maintenance logs, and deposits.
- Primary workflow: dispatch tool checkout risk scoring into a run report while respecting privacy-first constraints
- Signature interaction: constraint sliders that immediately explain route changes

## Required Shape
- First screen: Run Report workbench
- Hero controls: Dispatch, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: training status, maintenance logs, and deposits

## Service Boundary
- Keep run report state in a service; UI submits dispatch commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Router
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Route Whisperer for Maker-Space Tool Library' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: privacy-first workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for maker-space tool library and keep Route Whisperer as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Run Report workbench and keep the visible controls to Dispatch, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Run Report workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep run report state in a service; UI submits dispatch commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for training status, maintenance logs, and deposits so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of privacy-first workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces, Router with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Route Whisperer for Maker-Space Tool Library' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Route Whisperer for Maker-Space Tool Library to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for dispatch and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

Build Signal Sieve for Maker-Space Tool Library as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for maker-space tool library.
Use Signal Sieve as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic developer-tools templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: filters noisy intake into only the next action that matters for maker-space tool library, using training status, maintenance logs, and deposits.
- Primary workflow: assemble tool checkout risk scoring into a dispatch ticket while respecting time-sensitive constraints
- Signature interaction: incoming events fall into action buckets

## Required Shape
- First screen: Dispatch Ticket workbench
- Hero controls: Assemble, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: training status, maintenance logs, and deposits

## Service Boundary
- Keep dispatch ticket state in a service; UI submits assemble commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Agents
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Signal Sieve for Maker-Space Tool Library' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: time-sensitive workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for maker-space tool library and keep Signal Sieve as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Dispatch Ticket workbench and keep the visible controls to Assemble, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Dispatch Ticket workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep dispatch ticket state in a service; UI submits assemble commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for training status, maintenance logs, and deposits so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of time-sensitive workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces, Agents with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Signal Sieve for Maker-Space Tool Library' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Signal Sieve for Maker-Space Tool Library to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for assemble and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

- Why this exists: illuminates hidden deadline risk before it becomes urgent for wildfire defensible-space crew, using brush loads, owner permissions, and photo evidence.
- Primary workflow: recover parcel mitigation planning into a photo proof set while respecting route-aware constraints
- Signature interaction: risk beams connect tasks to time-sensitive blockers

- Hero controls: Recover, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: brush loads, owner permissions, and photo evidence

- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

# Recovery Rail for Food Truck Commissary Master Spec Prompt

Build Recovery Rail for Food Truck Commissary as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for food truck commissary.
Use Recovery Rail as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic hospitality templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: turns failed jobs into guided recovery paths for food truck commissary, using prep needs, sanitation logs, and fridge space.
- Primary workflow: simulate shared kitchen slot control into a risk memo while respecting audit-heavy constraints
- Signature interaction: failure cards branch into retry, reroute, or escalate

## Required Shape
- First screen: Risk Memo workbench
- Hero controls: Simulate, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: prep needs, sanitation logs, and fridge space

## Service Boundary
- Keep risk memo state in a service; UI submits simulate commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Agents
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Recovery Rail for Food Truck Commissary' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: audit-heavy workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for food truck commissary and keep Recovery Rail as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Risk Memo workbench and keep the visible controls to Simulate, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Risk Memo workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep risk memo state in a service; UI submits simulate commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for prep needs, sanitation logs, and fridge space so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of audit-heavy workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces, Agents with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Recovery Rail for Food Truck Commissary' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Recovery Rail for Food Truck Commissary to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for simulate and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

# Route Whisperer for Pop-Up Clinic Supply Cache Master Spec Prompt

Build Route Whisperer for Pop-Up Clinic Supply Cache as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for pop-up clinic supply cache.
Use Route Whisperer as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic health templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: turns conflicting constraints into a ranked route or assignment for pop-up clinic supply cache, using expiration dates, cold chain notes, and visit plans.
- Primary workflow: assemble field kit readiness into a route manifest while respecting role-scoped constraints
- Signature interaction: constraint sliders that immediately explain route changes

## Required Shape
- First screen: Route Manifest workbench
- Hero controls: Assemble, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: expiration dates, cold chain notes, and visit plans

## Service Boundary
- Keep route manifest state in a service; UI submits assemble commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Router, Agents
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Route Whisperer for Pop-Up Clinic Supply Cache' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: role-scoped workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for pop-up clinic supply cache and keep Route Whisperer as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Route Manifest workbench and keep the visible controls to Assemble, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Route Manifest workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep route manifest state in a service; UI submits assemble commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for expiration dates, cold chain notes, and visit plans so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of role-scoped workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces, Router, Agents with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Route Whisperer for Pop-Up Clinic Supply Cache' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Route Whisperer for Pop-Up Clinic Supply Cache to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for assemble and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

# Capacity Mirror for Pop-Up Clinic Supply Cache Master Spec Prompt

Build Capacity Mirror for Pop-Up Clinic Supply Cache as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for pop-up clinic supply cache.
Use Capacity Mirror as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic health templates.

- Why this exists: shows the real capacity picture before accepting new work for pop-up clinic supply cache, using expiration dates, cold chain notes, and visit plans.
- Primary workflow: simulate field kit readiness into a capacity board while respecting low-bandwidth constraints
- Signature interaction: capacity reflections by role, asset, or location

## Required Shape
- First screen: Capacity Board workbench
- Hero controls: Simulate, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: expiration dates, cold chain notes, and visit plans

## Service Boundary
- Keep capacity board state in a service; UI submits simulate commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Agents, Automations
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Capacity Mirror for Pop-Up Clinic Supply Cache' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: low-bandwidth workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for pop-up clinic supply cache and keep Capacity Mirror as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Capacity Board workbench and keep the visible controls to Simulate, Review, Save state.

- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Capacity Mirror for Pop-Up Clinic Supply Cache to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for simulate and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

Build Scenario Forge for Pop-Up Clinic Supply Cache as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for pop-up clinic supply cache.
Use Scenario Forge as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic health templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: builds small what-if trials before committing to a plan for pop-up clinic supply cache, using expiration dates, cold chain notes, and visit plans.
- Primary workflow: summarize field kit readiness into a fixture dataset while respecting multi-actor constraints
- Signature interaction: scenario tabs that compare assumptions side by side

## Required Shape
- First screen: Fixture Dataset workbench
- Hero controls: Summarize, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: expiration dates, cold chain notes, and visit plans

## Service Boundary
- Keep fixture dataset state in a service; UI submits summarize commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Models, Agents
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Scenario Forge for Pop-Up Clinic Supply Cache' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: multi-actor workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for pop-up clinic supply cache and keep Scenario Forge as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Fixture Dataset workbench and keep the visible controls to Summarize, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Fixture Dataset workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep fixture dataset state in a service; UI submits summarize commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for expiration dates, cold chain notes, and visit plans so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of multi-actor workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces, Models, Agents with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Scenario Forge for Pop-Up Clinic Supply Cache' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Scenario Forge for Pop-Up Clinic Supply Cache to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for summarize and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

# Workcell Lens for Trail Maintenance Guild Master Spec Prompt

Build Workcell Lens for Trail Maintenance Guild as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for trail maintenance guild.
Use Workcell Lens as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic public-sector templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: zooms from whole operation to the single blocked cell for trail maintenance guild, using trail segments, tools, and permit windows.
- Primary workflow: quote hazard-to-crew dispatch into a inventory snapshot while respecting multi-actor constraints
- Signature interaction: lens control drills from summary to one job

## Required Shape
- First screen: Inventory Snapshot workbench
- Hero controls: Quote, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: trail segments, tools, and permit windows

## Service Boundary
- Keep inventory snapshot state in a service; UI submits quote commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Settings
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Workcell Lens for Trail Maintenance Guild' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: multi-actor workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for trail segments, tools, and permit windows so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.

- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces, Settings with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Workcell Lens for Trail Maintenance Guild' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Workcell Lens for Trail Maintenance Guild to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for quote and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

- The first screen is focused and buildable.

- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.

# Scenario Forge for Neighborhood Solar Bulk-Buy Master Spec Prompt

Build Scenario Forge for Neighborhood Solar Bulk-Buy as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for neighborhood solar bulk-buy.
Use Scenario Forge as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic energy templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: builds small what-if trials before committing to a plan for neighborhood solar bulk-buy, using roof photos, utility bills, and contractor bids.
- Primary workflow: monitor quote cohort management into a exception log while respecting exception-driven constraints
- Signature interaction: scenario tabs that compare assumptions side by side

## Required Shape
- First screen: Exception Log workbench
- Hero controls: Monitor, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: roof photos, utility bills, and contractor bids

## Service Boundary
- Keep exception log state in a service; UI submits monitor commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Agents, Automations
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Scenario Forge for Neighborhood Solar Bulk-Buy' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: exception-driven workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for neighborhood solar bulk-buy and keep Scenario Forge as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Exception Log workbench and keep the visible controls to Monitor, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Exception Log workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep exception log state in a service; UI submits monitor commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for roof photos, utility bills, and contractor bids so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of exception-driven workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces, Agents, Automations with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Scenario Forge for Neighborhood Solar Bulk-Buy' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Scenario Forge for Neighborhood Solar Bulk-Buy to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for monitor and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

# Quiet Queue for Independent Comic Anthology Master Spec Prompt

Build Quiet Queue for Independent Comic Anthology as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for independent comic anthology.
Use Quiet Queue as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic creator templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: keeps messy work moving without noisy dashboards for independent comic anthology, using artists, lettering, and print deadlines.
- Primary workflow: handoff page progress orchestration into a compliance checklist while respecting low-bandwidth constraints
- Signature interaction: one calm queue that expands only when a decision is needed

## Required Shape
- First screen: Compliance Checklist workbench
- Hero controls: Handoff, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: artists, lettering, and print deadlines

## Service Boundary
- Keep compliance checklist state in a service; UI submits handoff commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Router
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Quiet Queue for Independent Comic Anthology' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: low-bandwidth workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for independent comic anthology and keep Quiet Queue as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Compliance Checklist workbench and keep the visible controls to Handoff, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Compliance Checklist workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep compliance checklist state in a service; UI submits handoff commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for artists, lettering, and print deadlines so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of low-bandwidth workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces, Router with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Quiet Queue for Independent Comic Anthology' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Quiet Queue for Independent Comic Anthology to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for handoff and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

Build Recovery Rail for Independent Comic Anthology as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for independent comic anthology.
Use Recovery Rail as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic creator templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: turns failed jobs into guided recovery paths for independent comic anthology, using artists, lettering, and print deadlines.
- Primary workflow: monitor page progress orchestration into a case timeline while respecting human-review-first constraints
- Signature interaction: failure cards branch into retry, reroute, or escalate

## Required Shape
- First screen: Case Timeline workbench
- Hero controls: Monitor, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: artists, lettering, and print deadlines

## Service Boundary
- Keep case timeline state in a service; UI submits monitor commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Automations
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Recovery Rail for Independent Comic Anthology' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: human-review-first workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for independent comic anthology and keep Recovery Rail as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Case Timeline workbench and keep the visible controls to Monitor, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Case Timeline workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep case timeline state in a service; UI submits monitor commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for artists, lettering, and print deadlines so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of human-review-first workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces, Automations with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Recovery Rail for Independent Comic Anthology' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Recovery Rail for Independent Comic Anthology to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for monitor and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

# Fixture Lab for Independent Comic Anthology Master Spec Prompt

Build Fixture Lab for Independent Comic Anthology as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for independent comic anthology.
Use Fixture Lab as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic creator templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: uses safe sample data to validate risky real-world workflows for independent comic anthology, using artists, lettering, and print deadlines.
- Primary workflow: quote page progress orchestration into a source bundle while respecting time-sensitive constraints
- Signature interaction: fixture switch toggles sample, synthetic, and live modes

## Required Shape
- First screen: Source Bundle workbench
- Hero controls: Quote, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: artists, lettering, and print deadlines

## Service Boundary
- Keep source bundle state in a service; UI submits quote commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Fixture Lab for Independent Comic Anthology' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: time-sensitive workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

- The first screen is focused and buildable.

- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.

Build Route Whisperer for Community Compost Pickup as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for community compost pickup.
Use Route Whisperer as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic climate templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: turns conflicting constraints into a ranked route or assignment for community compost pickup, using bucket weights, route photos, and education notes.
- Primary workflow: match contamination feedback loop into a compliance checklist while respecting offline-capable constraints
- Signature interaction: constraint sliders that immediately explain route changes

## Required Shape
- First screen: Compliance Checklist workbench
- Hero controls: Match, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: bucket weights, route photos, and education notes

## Service Boundary
- Keep compliance checklist state in a service; UI submits match commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Router
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Route Whisperer for Community Compost Pickup' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: offline-capable workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

- The first screen is focused and buildable.

# Evidence Loom for Mobile Bike Mechanic Master Spec Prompt

Build Evidence Loom for Mobile Bike Mechanic as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for mobile bike mechanic.
Use Evidence Loom as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic retail templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: weaves scattered proof into a single inspectable decision trail for mobile bike mechanic, using bike symptoms, stock, and travel time.
- Primary workflow: audit part-bin appointment planning into a compliance checklist while respecting route-aware constraints
- Signature interaction: drag evidence chips into a timeline and watch missing links glow

## Required Shape
- First screen: Compliance Checklist workbench
- Hero controls: Audit, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: bike symptoms, stock, and travel time

## Service Boundary
- Keep compliance checklist state in a service; UI submits audit commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Models
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Evidence Loom for Mobile Bike Mechanic' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: route-aware workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for mobile bike mechanic and keep Evidence Loom as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Compliance Checklist workbench and keep the visible controls to Audit, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Compliance Checklist workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep compliance checklist state in a service; UI submits audit commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for bike symptoms, stock, and travel time so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of route-aware workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces, Models with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Evidence Loom for Mobile Bike Mechanic' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Evidence Loom for Mobile Bike Mechanic to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for audit and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

Use Scenario Forge as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic retail templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: builds small what-if trials before committing to a plan for mobile bike mechanic, using bike symptoms, stock, and travel time.
- Primary workflow: recover part-bin appointment planning into a risk memo while respecting audit-heavy constraints
- Signature interaction: scenario tabs that compare assumptions side by side

## Required Shape
- First screen: Risk Memo workbench
- Hero controls: Recover, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: bike symptoms, stock, and travel time

## Service Boundary
- Keep risk memo state in a service; UI submits recover commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Router, Agents
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Scenario Forge for Mobile Bike Mechanic' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: audit-heavy workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for mobile bike mechanic and keep Scenario Forge as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Risk Memo workbench and keep the visible controls to Recover, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Risk Memo workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep risk memo state in a service; UI submits recover commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for bike symptoms, stock, and travel time so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of audit-heavy workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces, Router, Agents with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Scenario Forge for Mobile Bike Mechanic' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Scenario Forge for Mobile Bike Mechanic to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for recover and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

- The first screen is focused and buildable.

# Consent Compass for Public Mural Permitting Master Spec Prompt

Build Consent Compass for Public Mural Permitting as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for public mural permitting.
Use Consent Compass as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic public-sector templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: routes work based on allowed use, privacy, and authorization for public mural permitting, using wall owners, sketches, and neighborhood notices.
- Primary workflow: assemble site-to-artist approval flow into a risk memo while respecting privacy-first constraints
- Signature interaction: permission map that blocks unsafe actions

## Required Shape
- First screen: Risk Memo workbench
- Hero controls: Assemble, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: wall owners, sketches, and neighborhood notices

## Service Boundary
- Keep risk memo state in a service; UI submits assemble commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Agents
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Consent Compass for Public Mural Permitting' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: privacy-first workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for public mural permitting and keep Consent Compass as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Risk Memo workbench and keep the visible controls to Assemble, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Risk Memo workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep risk memo state in a service; UI submits assemble commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for wall owners, sketches, and neighborhood notices so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of privacy-first workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces, Agents with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Consent Compass for Public Mural Permitting' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Consent Compass for Public Mural Permitting to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for assemble and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

Use Recovery Rail as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic public-sector templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: turns failed jobs into guided recovery paths for public mural permitting, using wall owners, sketches, and neighborhood notices.
- Primary workflow: recover site-to-artist approval flow into a capacity board while respecting low-bandwidth constraints
- Signature interaction: failure cards branch into retry, reroute, or escalate

## Required Shape
- First screen: Capacity Board workbench
- Hero controls: Recover, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: wall owners, sketches, and neighborhood notices

## Service Boundary
- Keep capacity board state in a service; UI submits recover commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Router, Agents
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Recovery Rail for Public Mural Permitting' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: low-bandwidth workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for public mural permitting and keep Recovery Rail as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Capacity Board workbench and keep the visible controls to Recover, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Capacity Board workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep capacity board state in a service; UI submits recover commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for wall owners, sketches, and neighborhood notices so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of low-bandwidth workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces, Router, Agents with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Recovery Rail for Public Mural Permitting' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Recovery Rail for Public Mural Permitting to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for recover and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

Build Handoff Bell for Public Mural Permitting as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for public mural permitting.
Use Handoff Bell as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic public-sector templates.

- Why this exists: makes responsibility transfer explicit and auditable for public mural permitting, using wall owners, sketches, and neighborhood notices.

- Hero controls: Triage, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: wall owners, sketches, and neighborhood notices

- Keep run report state in a service; UI submits triage commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

- The first screen is focused and buildable.

# Route Whisperer for Wedding Micro-Venue Master Spec Prompt

Build Route Whisperer for Wedding Micro-Venue as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for wedding micro-venue.
Use Route Whisperer as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic hospitality templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: turns conflicting constraints into a ranked route or assignment for wedding micro-venue, using vendors, sound rules, and rain plans.
- Primary workflow: monitor timeline conflict guard into a exception log while respecting local-file backed constraints
- Signature interaction: constraint sliders that immediately explain route changes

## Required Shape
- First screen: Exception Log workbench
- Hero controls: Monitor, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: vendors, sound rules, and rain plans

## Service Boundary
- Keep exception log state in a service; UI submits monitor commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Router, Automations
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Route Whisperer for Wedding Micro-Venue' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: local-file backed workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for vendors, sound rules, and rain plans so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.

- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Route Whisperer for Wedding Micro-Venue to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for monitor and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.

- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.

# Evidence Loom for Board-Game Cafe League Master Spec Prompt

Build Evidence Loom for Board-Game Cafe League as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for board-game cafe league.
Use Evidence Loom as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic gaming templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: weaves scattered proof into a single inspectable decision trail for board-game cafe league, using players, games, and waitlists.
- Primary workflow: forecast table pairing and rules coaching into a exception log while respecting exception-driven constraints
- Signature interaction: drag evidence chips into a timeline and watch missing links glow

## Required Shape
- First screen: Exception Log workbench
- Hero controls: Forecast, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: players, games, and waitlists

## Service Boundary
- Keep exception log state in a service; UI submits forecast commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Automations
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Evidence Loom for Board-Game Cafe League' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: exception-driven workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for board-game cafe league and keep Evidence Loom as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Exception Log workbench and keep the visible controls to Forecast, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Exception Log workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep exception log state in a service; UI submits forecast commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for players, games, and waitlists so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of exception-driven workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces, Automations with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Evidence Loom for Board-Game Cafe League' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Evidence Loom for Board-Game Cafe League to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for forecast and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

Build Local Truth Desk for Language Exchange Club as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for language exchange club.
Use Local Truth Desk as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic education templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: prefers local files and service state over vague memory for language exchange club, using language goals, attendance, and topics.
- Primary workflow: simulate conversation pair rotation into a exception log while respecting exception-driven constraints
- Signature interaction: source badges on every generated answer

## Required Shape
- First screen: Exception Log workbench
- Hero controls: Simulate, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: language goals, attendance, and topics

## Service Boundary
- Keep exception log state in a service; UI submits simulate commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Models, Agents, Settings
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Local Truth Desk for Language Exchange Club' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: exception-driven workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for language exchange club and keep Local Truth Desk as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Exception Log workbench and keep the visible controls to Simulate, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Exception Log workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep exception log state in a service; UI submits simulate commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for language goals, attendance, and topics so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of exception-driven workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces, Models, Agents, Settings with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Local Truth Desk for Language Exchange Club' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Local Truth Desk for Language Exchange Club to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for simulate and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

# Scenario Forge for Small Port Chandlery Master Spec Prompt

Build Scenario Forge for Small Port Chandlery as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for small port chandlery.
Use Scenario Forge as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic retail templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: builds small what-if trials before committing to a plan for small port chandlery, using vessel types, part numbers, and tide deadlines.
- Primary workflow: audit boat-part request desk into a handoff card while respecting exception-driven constraints
- Signature interaction: scenario tabs that compare assumptions side by side

## Required Shape
- First screen: Handoff Card workbench
- Hero controls: Audit, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: vessel types, part numbers, and tide deadlines

## Service Boundary
- Keep handoff card state in a service; UI submits audit commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Models, Agents
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Scenario Forge for Small Port Chandlery' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: exception-driven workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for small port chandlery and keep Scenario Forge as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Handoff Card workbench and keep the visible controls to Audit, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Handoff Card workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep handoff card state in a service; UI submits audit commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for vessel types, part numbers, and tide deadlines so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of exception-driven workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces, Models, Agents with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Scenario Forge for Small Port Chandlery' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Scenario Forge for Small Port Chandlery to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for audit and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

Build Handoff Bell for Small Port Chandlery as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for small port chandlery.
Use Handoff Bell as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic retail templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: makes responsibility transfer explicit and auditable for small port chandlery, using vessel types, part numbers, and tide deadlines.
- Primary workflow: match boat-part request desk into a source bundle while respecting approval-gated constraints
- Signature interaction: handoff button creates a compact acceptance packet

## Required Shape
- First screen: Source Bundle workbench
- Hero controls: Match, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: vessel types, part numbers, and tide deadlines

## Service Boundary
- Keep source bundle state in a service; UI submits match commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Handoff Bell for Small Port Chandlery' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: approval-gated workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for small port chandlery and keep Handoff Bell as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Source Bundle workbench and keep the visible controls to Match, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Source Bundle workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep source bundle state in a service; UI submits match commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for vessel types, part numbers, and tide deadlines so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of approval-gated workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Handoff Bell for Small Port Chandlery' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Handoff Bell for Small Port Chandlery to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for match and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

Build Local Truth Desk for Quilting Guild Show as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for quilting guild show.
Use Local Truth Desk as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic creator templates.
