- Why this exists: prefers local files and service state over vague memory for quilting guild show, using quilt dimensions, categories, and judging notes.
- Primary workflow: match entry intake and display layout into a run report while respecting privacy-first constraints
- Signature interaction: source badges on every generated answer

## Required Shape
- First screen: Run Report workbench
- Hero controls: Match, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: quilt dimensions, categories, and judging notes

## Service Boundary
- Keep run report state in a service; UI submits match commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Models, Settings
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Local Truth Desk for Quilting Guild Show' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.

# Quiet Queue for Special Education Iep Binder Master Spec Prompt

Build Quiet Queue for Special Education Iep Binder as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for special education IEP binder.
Use Quiet Queue as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic education templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: keeps messy work moving without noisy dashboards for special education IEP binder, using goals, observations, and meeting history.
- Primary workflow: assemble evidence packet assembly into a case timeline while respecting time-sensitive constraints
- Signature interaction: one calm queue that expands only when a decision is needed

## Required Shape
- First screen: Case Timeline workbench
- Hero controls: Assemble, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: goals, observations, and meeting history

## Service Boundary
- Keep case timeline state in a service; UI submits assemble commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Agents
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Quiet Queue for Special Education Iep Binder' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: time-sensitive workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for special education IEP binder and keep Quiet Queue as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Case Timeline workbench and keep the visible controls to Assemble, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Case Timeline workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep case timeline state in a service; UI submits assemble commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for goals, observations, and meeting history so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of time-sensitive workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces, Agents with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Quiet Queue for Special Education Iep Binder' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Quiet Queue for Special Education Iep Binder to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for assemble and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

# Trust Ledger for Tenant Union Intake Master Spec Prompt

Build Trust Ledger for Tenant Union Intake as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for tenant union intake.
Use Trust Ledger as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic legal templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: shows who approved what and why before work moves forward for tenant union intake, using leases, photos, and landlord timelines.
- Primary workflow: handoff repair issue pattern detection into a run report while respecting model-assisted constraints
- Signature interaction: approval cards with source snapshots

## Required Shape
- First screen: Run Report workbench
- Hero controls: Handoff, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: leases, photos, and landlord timelines

## Service Boundary
- Keep run report state in a service; UI submits handoff commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Router
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Trust Ledger for Tenant Union Intake' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: model-assisted workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for tenant union intake and keep Trust Ledger as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Run Report workbench and keep the visible controls to Handoff, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Run Report workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep run report state in a service; UI submits handoff commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for leases, photos, and landlord timelines so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of model-assisted workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces, Router with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Trust Ledger for Tenant Union Intake' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Trust Ledger for Tenant Union Intake to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for handoff and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

Build Proof Garden for Tenant Union Intake as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for tenant union intake.
Use Proof Garden as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic legal templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: lets evidence grow from rough notes into validated records for tenant union intake, using leases, photos, and landlord timelines.
- Primary workflow: plan repair issue pattern detection into a dispatch ticket while respecting approval-gated constraints
- Signature interaction: seed notes become verified cards after checks

## Required Shape
- First screen: Dispatch Ticket workbench
- Hero controls: Plan, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: leases, photos, and landlord timelines

## Service Boundary
- Keep dispatch ticket state in a service; UI submits plan commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Proof Garden for Tenant Union Intake' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: approval-gated workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for tenant union intake and keep Proof Garden as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Dispatch Ticket workbench and keep the visible controls to Plan, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Dispatch Ticket workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep dispatch ticket state in a service; UI submits plan commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for leases, photos, and landlord timelines so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of approval-gated workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Proof Garden for Tenant Union Intake' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Proof Garden for Tenant Union Intake to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for plan and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

# Fixture Lab for Micro-Insurance Claims Desk Master Spec Prompt

Build Fixture Lab for Micro-Insurance Claims Desk as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for micro-insurance claims desk.
Use Fixture Lab as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic finance templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: uses safe sample data to validate risky real-world workflows for micro-insurance claims desk, using receipts, photos, and coverage rules.
- Primary workflow: quote low-value claim evidence review into a source bundle while respecting human-review-first constraints
- Signature interaction: fixture switch toggles sample, synthetic, and live modes

## Required Shape
- First screen: Source Bundle workbench
- Hero controls: Quote, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: receipts, photos, and coverage rules

## Service Boundary
- Keep source bundle state in a service; UI submits quote commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Fixture Lab for Micro-Insurance Claims Desk' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: human-review-first workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for micro-insurance claims desk and keep Fixture Lab as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Source Bundle workbench and keep the visible controls to Quote, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Source Bundle workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep source bundle state in a service; UI submits quote commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for receipts, photos, and coverage rules so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of human-review-first workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Fixture Lab for Micro-Insurance Claims Desk' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Fixture Lab for Micro-Insurance Claims Desk to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for quote and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

Build Route Whisperer for Farmers Market Token Booth as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for farmers market token booth.

- First screen: Photo Proof Set workbench
- Hero controls: Plan, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals

- Keep photo proof set state in a service; UI submits plan commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Router

- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.

Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

# Pocket Ops Room for Machine Shop Quote Cell Master Spec Prompt

Build Pocket Ops Room for Machine Shop Quote Cell as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for machine shop quote cell.
Use Pocket Ops Room as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic manufacturing templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: compresses a full back office into a field-ready workflow for machine shop quote cell, using materials, tolerances, and machine capacity.
- Primary workflow: audit drawing-to-estimate workflow into a inventory snapshot while respecting role-scoped constraints
- Signature interaction: offline-first job packet with later sync review

## Required Shape
- First screen: Inventory Snapshot workbench
- Hero controls: Audit, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: materials, tolerances, and machine capacity

## Service Boundary
- Keep inventory snapshot state in a service; UI submits audit commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Models, Settings
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Pocket Ops Room for Machine Shop Quote Cell' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: role-scoped workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for machine shop quote cell and keep Pocket Ops Room as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Inventory Snapshot workbench and keep the visible controls to Audit, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Inventory Snapshot workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep inventory snapshot state in a service; UI submits audit commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for materials, tolerances, and machine capacity so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of role-scoped workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces, Models, Settings with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Pocket Ops Room for Machine Shop Quote Cell' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Pocket Ops Room for Machine Shop Quote Cell to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for audit and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

Build Handoff Bell for Last-Mile Medicine Courier as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for last-mile medicine courier.
Use Handoff Bell as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic logistics templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: makes responsibility transfer explicit and auditable for last-mile medicine courier, using cooler telemetry, signatures, and exceptions.
- Primary workflow: recover temperature-sensitive route proof into a exception log while respecting exception-driven constraints
- Signature interaction: handoff button creates a compact acceptance packet

## Required Shape
- First screen: Exception Log workbench
- Hero controls: Recover, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: cooler telemetry, signatures, and exceptions

## Service Boundary
- Keep exception log state in a service; UI submits recover commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Router, Agents
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Handoff Bell for Last-Mile Medicine Courier' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: exception-driven workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for last-mile medicine courier and keep Handoff Bell as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Exception Log workbench and keep the visible controls to Recover, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Exception Log workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep exception log state in a service; UI submits recover commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for cooler telemetry, signatures, and exceptions so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of exception-driven workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces, Router, Agents with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Handoff Bell for Last-Mile Medicine Courier' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Handoff Bell for Last-Mile Medicine Courier to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for recover and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

# Route Treaty for Last-Mile Medicine Courier Master Spec Prompt

Build Route Treaty for Last-Mile Medicine Courier as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for last-mile medicine courier.
Use Route Treaty as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic logistics templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: makes competing route rules visible and negotiable for last-mile medicine courier, using cooler telemetry, signatures, and exceptions.
- Primary workflow: triage temperature-sensitive route proof into a inventory snapshot while respecting role-scoped constraints
- Signature interaction: rule cards vote on the next route

## Required Shape
- First screen: Inventory Snapshot workbench
- Hero controls: Triage, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: cooler telemetry, signatures, and exceptions

## Service Boundary
- Keep inventory snapshot state in a service; UI submits triage commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Router
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Route Treaty for Last-Mile Medicine Courier' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: role-scoped workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for last-mile medicine courier and keep Route Treaty as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Inventory Snapshot workbench and keep the visible controls to Triage, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Inventory Snapshot workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep inventory snapshot state in a service; UI submits triage commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for cooler telemetry, signatures, and exceptions so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of role-scoped workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces, Router with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Route Treaty for Last-Mile Medicine Courier' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Route Treaty for Last-Mile Medicine Courier to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for triage and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

Build Consent Compass for Home Energy Audit Crew as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for home energy audit crew.
Use Consent Compass as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic energy templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: routes work based on allowed use, privacy, and authorization for home energy audit crew, using blower-door notes, rebates, and contractor bids.
- Primary workflow: quote retrofit recommendation planner into a estimate sheet while respecting low-bandwidth constraints
- Signature interaction: permission map that blocks unsafe actions

## Required Shape
- First screen: Estimate Sheet workbench
- Hero controls: Quote, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: blower-door notes, rebates, and contractor bids

## Service Boundary
- Keep estimate sheet state in a service; UI submits quote commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Consent Compass for Home Energy Audit Crew' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: low-bandwidth workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for home energy audit crew and keep Consent Compass as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Estimate Sheet workbench and keep the visible controls to Quote, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Estimate Sheet workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep estimate sheet state in a service; UI submits quote commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for blower-door notes, rebates, and contractor bids so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of low-bandwidth workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Consent Compass for Home Energy Audit Crew' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Consent Compass for Home Energy Audit Crew to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for quote and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

Build Friction Map for Home Energy Audit Crew as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for home energy audit crew.
Use Friction Map as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic energy templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: surfaces where a workflow keeps stalling for home energy audit crew, using blower-door notes, rebates, and contractor bids.
- Primary workflow: triage retrofit recommendation planner into a source bundle while respecting approval-gated constraints
- Signature interaction: heatmap over steps, approvals, and missing inputs

## Required Shape
- First screen: Source Bundle workbench
- Hero controls: Triage, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: blower-door notes, rebates, and contractor bids

## Service Boundary
- Keep source bundle state in a service; UI submits triage commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Router
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Friction Map for Home Energy Audit Crew' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: approval-gated workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for home energy audit crew and keep Friction Map as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Source Bundle workbench and keep the visible controls to Triage, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Source Bundle workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep source bundle state in a service; UI submits triage commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for blower-door notes, rebates, and contractor bids so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of approval-gated workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces, Router with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Friction Map for Home Energy Audit Crew' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Friction Map for Home Energy Audit Crew to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for triage and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

- Keep operator brief state in a service; UI submits handoff commands and subscribes to progress.

# Capacity Mirror for Neighborhood Camera Registry Master Spec Prompt

Build Capacity Mirror for Neighborhood Camera Registry as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for neighborhood camera registry.
Use Capacity Mirror as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic security templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: shows the real capacity picture before accepting new work for neighborhood camera registry, using camera owners, time windows, and approvals.
- Primary workflow: plan warrant-safe request tracking into a exception log while respecting exception-driven constraints
- Signature interaction: capacity reflections by role, asset, or location

## Required Shape
- First screen: Exception Log workbench
- Hero controls: Plan, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: camera owners, time windows, and approvals

## Service Boundary
- Keep exception log state in a service; UI submits plan commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Automations
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Capacity Mirror for Neighborhood Camera Registry' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: exception-driven workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for neighborhood camera registry and keep Capacity Mirror as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Exception Log workbench and keep the visible controls to Plan, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Exception Log workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep exception log state in a service; UI submits plan commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for camera owners, time windows, and approvals so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of exception-driven workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces, Automations with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Capacity Mirror for Neighborhood Camera Registry' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Capacity Mirror for Neighborhood Camera Registry to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for plan and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

Use Fixture Lab as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic developer-tools templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: uses safe sample data to validate risky real-world workflows for open-source maintainer desk, using issues, labels, tests, and changelogs.
- Primary workflow: schedule issue-to-release triage into a run report while respecting model-assisted constraints
- Signature interaction: fixture switch toggles sample, synthetic, and live modes

## Required Shape
- First screen: Run Report workbench
- Hero controls: Schedule, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: issues, labels, tests, and changelogs

## Service Boundary
- Keep run report state in a service; UI submits schedule commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Automations
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Fixture Lab for Open-Source Maintainer Desk' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: model-assisted workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for open-source maintainer desk and keep Fixture Lab as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Run Report workbench and keep the visible controls to Schedule, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Run Report workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep run report state in a service; UI submits schedule commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for issues, labels, tests, and changelogs so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of model-assisted workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces, Automations with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Fixture Lab for Open-Source Maintainer Desk' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Fixture Lab for Open-Source Maintainer Desk to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for schedule and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

# Workcell Lens for Api Migration Studio Master Spec Prompt

Build Workcell Lens for Api Migration Studio as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for API migration studio.
Use Workcell Lens as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic developer-tools templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: zooms from whole operation to the single blocked cell for API migration studio, using endpoints, clients, and deprecation dates.
- Primary workflow: review integration breakage mapping into a recovery note while respecting privacy-first constraints
- Signature interaction: lens control drills from summary to one job

## Required Shape
- First screen: Recovery Note workbench
- Hero controls: Review, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: endpoints, clients, and deprecation dates

## Service Boundary
- Keep recovery note state in a service; UI submits review commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Models, Settings
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Workcell Lens for Api Migration Studio' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: privacy-first workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for API migration studio and keep Workcell Lens as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Recovery Note workbench and keep the visible controls to Review, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Recovery Note workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep recovery note state in a service; UI submits review commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for endpoints, clients, and deprecation dates so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of privacy-first workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces, Models, Settings with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Workcell Lens for Api Migration Studio' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Workcell Lens for Api Migration Studio to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for review and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

# Continuity Thread for Model Evaluation Bench Master Spec Prompt

Build Continuity Thread for Model Evaluation Bench as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for model evaluation bench.
Use Continuity Thread as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic ai-ops templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: keeps handoffs consistent across people, places, and sessions for model evaluation bench, using datasets, metrics, and run artifacts.
- Primary workflow: plan prompt regression comparison into a capacity board while respecting route-aware constraints
- Signature interaction: threaded handoff cards with before/after snapshots

## Required Shape
- First screen: Capacity Board workbench
- Hero controls: Plan, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: datasets, metrics, and run artifacts

## Service Boundary
- Keep capacity board state in a service; UI submits plan commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Continuity Thread for Model Evaluation Bench' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: route-aware workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for model evaluation bench and keep Continuity Thread as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Capacity Board workbench and keep the visible controls to Plan, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Capacity Board workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep capacity board state in a service; UI submits plan commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for datasets, metrics, and run artifacts so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of route-aware workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Continuity Thread for Model Evaluation Bench' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Continuity Thread for Model Evaluation Bench to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for plan and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

# Scenario Forge for Model Evaluation Bench Master Spec Prompt

Build Scenario Forge for Model Evaluation Bench as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for model evaluation bench.
Use Scenario Forge as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic ai-ops templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: builds small what-if trials before committing to a plan for model evaluation bench, using datasets, metrics, and run artifacts.
- Primary workflow: match prompt regression comparison into a compliance checklist while respecting low-bandwidth constraints
- Signature interaction: scenario tabs that compare assumptions side by side

## Required Shape
- First screen: Compliance Checklist workbench
- Hero controls: Match, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: datasets, metrics, and run artifacts

## Service Boundary
- Keep compliance checklist state in a service; UI submits match commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Agents
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Scenario Forge for Model Evaluation Bench' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: low-bandwidth workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for model evaluation bench and keep Scenario Forge as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Compliance Checklist workbench and keep the visible controls to Match, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Compliance Checklist workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep compliance checklist state in a service; UI submits match commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for datasets, metrics, and run artifacts so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of low-bandwidth workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces, Agents with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Scenario Forge for Model Evaluation Bench' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Scenario Forge for Model Evaluation Bench to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for match and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

Build Deadline Lantern for Seasonal Hiring Desk as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for seasonal hiring desk.
Use Deadline Lantern as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic hr templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: illuminates hidden deadline risk before it becomes urgent for seasonal hiring desk, using candidates, documents, and training slots.
- Primary workflow: audit availability-to-shift matching into a approval packet while respecting human-review-first constraints
- Signature interaction: risk beams connect tasks to time-sensitive blockers

## Required Shape
- First screen: Approval Packet workbench
- Hero controls: Audit, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: candidates, documents, and training slots

## Service Boundary
- Keep approval packet state in a service; UI submits audit commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Models, Automations
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Deadline Lantern for Seasonal Hiring Desk' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: human-review-first workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for seasonal hiring desk and keep Deadline Lantern as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Approval Packet workbench and keep the visible controls to Audit, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Approval Packet workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep approval packet state in a service; UI submits audit commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for candidates, documents, and training slots so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of human-review-first workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces, Models, Automations with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Deadline Lantern for Seasonal Hiring Desk' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Deadline Lantern for Seasonal Hiring Desk to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for audit and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

- Hero controls: Assemble, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: candidates, documents, and training slots

- Keep fixture dataset state in a service; UI submits assemble commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

# Pocket Ops Room for Employee Accommodations Office Master Spec Prompt

Build Pocket Ops Room for Employee Accommodations Office as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for employee accommodations office.
Use Pocket Ops Room as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic hr templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: compresses a full back office into a field-ready workflow for employee accommodations office, using needs, approvals, and privacy notes.
- Primary workflow: route case-safe request tracking into a approval packet while respecting time-sensitive constraints
- Signature interaction: offline-first job packet with later sync review

## Required Shape
- First screen: Approval Packet workbench
- Hero controls: Route, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: needs, approvals, and privacy notes

## Service Boundary
- Keep approval packet state in a service; UI submits route commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces, Router, Settings
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Pocket Ops Room for Employee Accommodations Office' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: time-sensitive workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for employee accommodations office and keep Pocket Ops Room as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Approval Packet workbench and keep the visible controls to Route, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Approval Packet workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep approval packet state in a service; UI submits route commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for needs, approvals, and privacy notes so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of time-sensitive workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces, Router, Settings with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Pocket Ops Room for Employee Accommodations Office' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Pocket Ops Room for Employee Accommodations Office to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for route and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.
